content: 1. Latex or polyurethane condoms and dental dams should be used during sexual activity to reduce the risk of spreading infections, including HIV. 2. If you miss a dose of cidofovir, it is crucial to contact your doctor or pharmacist immediately to establish a new dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. 3. If you miss a dose of probenecid, inform your doctor or pharmacist right away. 4. For proper storage of this medication, refer to the product instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly. 5. Before using cidofovir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other antivirals (e.g., ganciclovir), probenecid, or sulfa drugs (e.g., sulfamethoxazole), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. 8. Cidofovir may cause vision changes. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring clear vision until you are confident you can do so safely. 9. During pregnancy, cidofovir should only be used when clearly necessary, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. The manufacturer advises avoiding pregnancy during treatment. Men with female partners should use effective barrier protection (e.g., latex or polyurethane condoms) during treatment and for at least 90 days after stopping the medication. 10. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. If you have HIV, breastfeeding may transmit the virus to your baby. 11. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 12. Avoid taking other medications that may harm your kidneys (e.g., amphotericin B, foscarnet, pentamidine, vancomycin, aminoglycosides like tobramycin, or NSAIDs like ibuprofen) within 7 days before and during treatment with this medication. Serious, potentially fatal kidney damage may occur in some cases. Check the labels of all your medications for NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen). 13. In case of an overdose with serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. 14. Regular lab and/or medical tests (e.g., eye exams) should be conducted while using this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. 15. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, always use effective barrier methods (e.g., latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams) during sexual activity. 16.
